Forest Village Rules

Gather clay, seeds and feathers, place workers and build a forest village. Production triggers after every second worker placed.

The rules

Resources and the forest
There are three resources: clay, seeds and feathers. The forest offers six resource spaces and two shared card spaces.
A turn
On your turn you do one thing: send a free squirrel into the forest, or build one card, or – when all your squirrels are out – change the season. Then it is the next player's turn. Each player moves through the seasons at their own pace.
Buildings and animals
Build from your hand or from the Clearing, where 6 cards are open; a taken card is replaced at once. Each animal pairs with a building and costs one feather less when that building is in your village. Production cards pay when built and after every second worker placed. A village holds at most 12 cards and a hand 8.
Seasons
When all your squirrels are out, you may change the season: the squirrels come back, then spring brings 1 more squirrel, summer 2 cards, autumn 2 more squirrels. Production is triggered after every second worker you place, regardless of season. Winter is the last season: when you can or want to do nothing more, tap Done for this game.
End and points
The game ends when everyone is done with winter. Points come from the cards in your village, 2 points for every pair (a building with its animal), the end bonuses of some cards and the task card: one task lies open each game, and everyone who fulfils it at the end gets its points. Players who start later get more cards at the start (5, 6, 7 and 8).
Alone
With 1 player you play the same rules and win if you have at least 45 points at the end.
Playing
Tap a free field of the forest to send a squirrel there. Tap a card in your hand or in the Clearing to read it, then Build; cards you cannot pay for now say so. The list below shows the last moves, including the computer's. Against the computer: Easy often plays at random, Medium builds what looks best now, Hard also plans for the animals and the end. On one device the hand is covered between turns.

Example

You pay 2 clay and 1 feather for the Bakery. It gives 2 feathers when built and again after your second worker. Later the Hedgehog costs one feather less because its Bakery is in your village.
